name: Battery tray with strap slots and the bay board hold-down springs
note: Four corner bosses and four pads seat the pack at z 37; four M3 × 6 countersunk machine screws into M3 heat-set inserts in P_base (heads 1.5 mm under the pack, 3.5 mm thread engagement). Floor and side walls trimmed to |y| <= 71 for x -115.5..-100.5, under the rear cliff sensor boards: with the battery and the screws out it slides 2 mm aft and lifts straight out. The front wall carries 3 compliant hold-down fingers on its front wall (CAD id bay_holddown; at y 39.28, 4.59, -14.23, in the gaps of the bay board's rear connector row): each hangs from the free end of a 31 mm cantilever cut out of the wall (wall raised to z 43 over it; it bends vertically, within the layers), reaches 1.95 mm over the board's rear edge (flat contact 0.8 mm, then a 1.15 × 45° lead-in under the tip) and rests 0.35 mm below the board top, so the board lifts it by that much and it holds the rear edge down on the ribs with 2.53 N (0.36–4.7 N over the ±0.3 mm design stack-up: rib, pocket, board 1.6 ± 0.16, tray floor, print tolerance; RSS 0.275 mm), root bending stress <= 10.5 MPa (21 % of a 50 MPa PETG yield; a Ø1.5 mm keyhole relief at each beam root keeps the local peak near 22.1 MPa, Kt about 1.8–2.1, an estimate). At the linear worst case (all six tolerances at their limits at once, ±0.66 mm, unlikely but possible): a finger can stand up to 0.31 mm off the board (no hold-down there until shimmed), or its beam bends to 16.3 MPa (33 % of yield, local peak about 34.2 MPa). The 1.15 mm lead-in clears the board corner even there (1.11 mm needed; 0.75 mm at the design stack), so a finger rides up instead of jamming. After printing, free the beams: run a fine razor saw (kerf <= 0.5 mm) along each of the three 0.6 mm slots under them, cutting its 10 breakaway posts, so each beam springs freely. Fit the tray after the board: set it 2 mm aft of its place and slide it forward, the fingers riding up their lead-ins onto the board top. Check: each finger stands lifted about 0.35 mm off its rest, and a 0.05 mm feeler does not pass under its tip. If it does, either the board is not seated on the ribs, a post is left, or the stack-up ran to the low end: then stick 0.1 mm PTFE tape (F03) under that finger's tip, a layer at a time (about 0.3 mm at most), until the feeler no longer passes (the shim remedy for visible play). The STL is the tray as printed (one part, floor down, no supports).

name: Power & I/O bay board: the routed 4-layer board with its fitted parts (pcb/fab/r1_power_io.step)
note: KiCad fab STEP (pcb/fab/r1_power_io.step, robot = STEP + (-66.5, 50, 35.4)): the laminate and every fitted part model (the J1 XT30, J2 JST VH and J3 Micro-Fit headers, the FLR fuse holders and C1 as their envelopes), copper skins and via barrels left out; THT leads cut at 1.4 mm under the board (z 34: the assembly trims them to <= 1.4 mm, 1.0 mm over the base top); D1 at its PARTS h (STEP heights: max(model, PARTS h)). Outline x -66.4..7.5, |y| <= 50 (tongue |y| <= 33.4 for x > -13.8), z 35.4–37; on four 2.4 mm printed PETG spacers with M3 × 8 pan-head screws into heat-set inserts at (-19.5, 38), (-19.5, -38), (-11.5, 8.5), (-11.5, -8.5) (Ø3.2 holes), and clamped at (-33, 40), (-33, -46) (Ø3 NPTH, ruling PB3) between a printed clamp spacer and a rear 20 mm Jetson standoff; its rear edge held down by 3 fingers on the battery tray wall. Height zones: under the carrier (x >= -38.5) every part top, including a mated plug and its wire bend, <= z 53.27 (16.27 mm over the board top); behind it (x < -38.5) <= z 97.5 (lid underside - 3 mm), exposed with the lid off. Assembly order (bay board under the Jetson): 0. on the bench, make the two motor pigtails (C18) and plug them on. They differ in length and in pin-1 order, so tag each one "L / J4" (left motor) or "R / J5" (right motor) right after making it, before it is plugged on. The pre-cut length of the six wires of each pigtail is 61 mm for J4 (left) and 57 mm for J5 (right): the drawn route + terminations + the full 12.7 mm pin spread, rounded up to the mm, because the six wires fan out 6.35 mm either side of the bundle's centre line at both ends (the socket's six sleeves and the male housing's six cavities each span 12.7 mm). Solder the socket end first (one wire lapped on each solder tail of the right-angle socket under its Ø1.8 sleeve, red wire on pin 1, the tails and wires pointing up), then push the socket onto its header; leave the male ends long: they are dressed along the route, trimmed to length and crimped in step 4. J4 pin 1 = rear end, J5 pin 1 = front end (the square pads); the pigtails are built alike, so the rule is the same for both: looking into the socket's mating face with its tails up, the red wire (pin 1) is on the left. The pigtails stay with the board. Power connectors (ruling PB30): the battery (J1, an AMASS XT30 PCB male), the master rocker (J2, a JST VH header) and the Jetson 5 V (J3, a Molex Micro-Fit 3.0 right-angle header) are three different connector families, so no lead fits a wrong header; tag the three leads anyway ("J1 BATT", "J2 ROCKER", "J3 JETSON 5V") right after making them. Battery lead polarity: J1 pin 1 is GND (silk "-") and pin 2 is BAT+ (silk "+"), so the lead's XT30U-F carries GND in cavity 1 (its "-" contact: battery -, black) and BAT+ in cavity 2 (its "+" contact: battery +, red); the XT30 mates only one way round, but a lead soldered the wrong way round still mates. Check it fail-safe before the fuses go in: with F1 and F2 out, plug W01 into J1 and into the battery and measure F1's input clip (its BAT+ side, F1 pin 1) against a GND pad (TP5 or an M3 hole ring): it must read positive, about the pack voltage (≥ 6 V; a part-discharged pack reads lower); a reversed lead reads negative and, with the fuses out, has no current path. Only then fit the fuses, always with the rocker off (F1 first, F2 last): a reversed lead with the fuses in is the costliest mistake on this board (it has no reverse-polarity protection); 1. bond the two printed bearing ribs into their 0.6 mm locating pockets in the P_base top with epoxy (F04) and let it cure; fit the two front Jetson standoffs (24 mm stacks), screwed from below; 2. set the four 2.4 mm printed spacers and the two printed clamp spacers on P_base, lower the bay board onto them and screw it down with four M3 × 8 pan-head screws into the inserts; 3. fit the battery tray (its hold-down beams freed: breakaway posts cut): set it 2 mm aft of its place, slide it forward so its three spring fingers ride up their lead-ins onto the board's top face between the rear connectors, screw it down, and check each finger stands lifted: a 0.05 mm feeler does not pass under its tip; if it does, that finger has play (it is off the board): stick 0.1 mm PTFE tape (F03) under its tip as a shim, a layer at a time (about 0.3 mm at most), until the feeler no longer passes; 4. plug the under-carrier cables. Pigtails: dress each one as drawn, with no slack (it rides up with the board when the joint is unplugged): straight up out of the socket, toward the front about 12 mm over the board beside U5A (J9 on the right), out between the P03 and the motor face, and down to the inline joint just ahead of the motor (x 15.2..17.8, |y| 38..60); then trim each wire at its own cavity of the male housing (finished lengths 35.4–60.8 mm for J4 and 31.1–56.5 mm for J5, set by where each wire sits at both ends) and crimp its male pin into the 1×6 housing, red wire = pin 1. Factory cables: measure each one from the encoder cap to the female housing's rear face (the wire entry); readings of 186–200 mm all fit (2–3 turns), and a longer cable up to 220 mm still fits (up to 3.5 turns). Route the fixed path first (about 89 mm outside the coil): a flat row along the motor's inner end face toward the rear, round the motor's rear shoulder and forward over the motor top (never over the pigtail), down the motor's front shoulder under the bumper lead, and from the coil position into the housing; wind the remainder (the measured length less the fixed path: 97–111 mm) into the coil on the base ahead of the motor (2–3.5 turns, about 16 mm across, at x 25, |y| 72) and tie it through its two slots. Then mate each motor's factory female housing onto its pigtail's male housing: the joint is not keyed, so mate the pin-1 stripe to the pin-1 stripe (both halves are marked at the red wire) and check the colours run straight across; stand the joint on the base and tie it down with a cable tie down the motor opening and up through the slot beside it; bumpers J10/J11; front cliffs J8/J9; 5. set and verify the P03 output voltage on the bench, connect it to U5A/U5B (pin 1 is "+" on both terminals, silk "+", the screw nearer the robot centre line: U5A.1 to P03 IN+, U5B.1 to P03 OUT+, red wires on pin 1), then fit it on its foam tape in the front bay with the cable tie through the P_base slots at (28, ±33.3); before the Jetson is connected (W04 unplugged): battery in, F1 fitted, rocker on, and measure against a GND pad: U5A.1 reads positive, about the pack voltage, and U5B.1 positive 5.1 V (0 V or negative: the P03 leads are swapped or loose); then rocker off; 6. stand the two rear 20 mm F-F standoffs on the board and screw each down with an M2.5 × 12 countersunk screw from under P_base through the base, the clamp spacer and the board (they clamp the board); 7. fit the Jetson (four M2.5 top screws), then its six plugs; before the 5 V barrel plug goes in, check the Jetson lead W04 on J3 with its barrel plug free and the rocker on: the plug's centre reads positive 5.1 V against its sleeve (negative: the two Micro-Fit crimps are swapped), then rocker off and plug it in. Service: step 0, every time, before reaching inside: shut the Jetson down, switch the rocker off and unplug the battery (BAT+ is live and unfused at F1's input whenever the battery is plugged in). Everyday rule: the rocker off before plugging or unplugging the battery; shut the Jetson down before switching the rocker off; fit or pull a fuse only with the rocker off (rocker off, fit F2, rocker on). With the lid off, the board's rear band (Pico USB, rear connector row, the Jetson 5 V lead J3, fuses) is reachable; the motor inline joints, the other under-carrier connectors and the P03 (tie, trimpot) need the Jetson off (its six plugs: camera, LiDAR and Pico USB, Wi-Fi dongle, 5 V barrel plug, fan; then its four top screws). To take the board out: Jetson off; the two rear standoffs off (their M2.5 screws from under P_base); the battery out (strap, Tamiya plug); the four tray screws out, the tray slid 2 mm aft and lifted straight out (its springs come off the board edge; its walls are cut clear of the rear cliff sensor boards); the four M3 board screws out; unplug the rear-band plugs, the motor inline joints (loosen each factory-cable coil tie first: the 8 mm each housing slides back comes out of the coil; then cut the joint ties and slide each factory housing off its pigtail; the pigtails stay on J4 / J5 and ride up with the board), the bumper and front cliff leads and the P03 leads; lift the board. Fit new ties when it goes back (retie the coils).

name: P03 5 V converter envelope (62 × 38 × 14 mm) on foam tape
note: Measured envelope 62 × 38 × 14 mm on 1 mm double-sided foam tape (z 33–48), turned 90 deg: long side along y, x 9..47, |y| <= 31, in the front bay under the front of the Jetson carrier, ahead of the bay board's tongue (x 7.5) and aft of the bumper riders B at full travel (validation p03_clear_of_bumper_travel). A cable tie over it through the P_base slots at (28, ±33.3) holds it. Leads to U5A/U5B on the tongue's front edge, about 10 mm. Its tie and trimpot are reachable only before the Jetson goes on. Assembly order (bay board under the Jetson): 0. on the bench, make the two motor pigtails (C18) and plug them on. They differ in length and in pin-1 order, so tag each one "L / J4" (left motor) or "R / J5" (right motor) right after making it, before it is plugged on. The pre-cut length of the six wires of each pigtail is 61 mm for J4 (left) and 57 mm for J5 (right): the drawn route + terminations + the full 12.7 mm pin spread, rounded up to the mm, because the six wires fan out 6.35 mm either side of the bundle's centre line at both ends (the socket's six sleeves and the male housing's six cavities each span 12.7 mm). Solder the socket end first (one wire lapped on each solder tail of the right-angle socket under its Ø1.8 sleeve, red wire on pin 1, the tails and wires pointing up), then push the socket onto its header; leave the male ends long: they are dressed along the route, trimmed to length and crimped in step 4. J4 pin 1 = rear end, J5 pin 1 = front end (the square pads); the pigtails are built alike, so the rule is the same for both: looking into the socket's mating face with its tails up, the red wire (pin 1) is on the left. The pigtails stay with the board. Power connectors (ruling PB30): the battery (J1, an AMASS XT30 PCB male), the master rocker (J2, a JST VH header) and the Jetson 5 V (J3, a Molex Micro-Fit 3.0 right-angle header) are three different connector families, so no lead fits a wrong header; tag the three leads anyway ("J1 BATT", "J2 ROCKER", "J3 JETSON 5V") right after making them. Battery lead polarity: J1 pin 1 is GND (silk "-") and pin 2 is BAT+ (silk "+"), so the lead's XT30U-F carries GND in cavity 1 (its "-" contact: battery -, black) and BAT+ in cavity 2 (its "+" contact: battery +, red); the XT30 mates only one way round, but a lead soldered the wrong way round still mates. Check it fail-safe before the fuses go in: with F1 and F2 out, plug W01 into J1 and into the battery and measure F1's input clip (its BAT+ side, F1 pin 1) against a GND pad (TP5 or an M3 hole ring): it must read positive, about the pack voltage (≥ 6 V; a part-discharged pack reads lower); a reversed lead reads negative and, with the fuses out, has no current path. Only then fit the fuses, always with the rocker off (F1 first, F2 last): a reversed lead with the fuses in is the costliest mistake on this board (it has no reverse-polarity protection); 1. bond the two printed bearing ribs into their 0.6 mm locating pockets in the P_base top with epoxy (F04) and let it cure; fit the two front Jetson standoffs (24 mm stacks), screwed from below; 2. set the four 2.4 mm printed spacers and the two printed clamp spacers on P_base, lower the bay board onto them and screw it down with four M3 × 8 pan-head screws into the inserts; 3. fit the battery tray (its hold-down beams freed: breakaway posts cut): set it 2 mm aft of its place, slide it forward so its three spring fingers ride up their lead-ins onto the board's top face between the rear connectors, screw it down, and check each finger stands lifted: a 0.05 mm feeler does not pass under its tip; if it does, that finger has play (it is off the board): stick 0.1 mm PTFE tape (F03) under its tip as a shim, a layer at a time (about 0.3 mm at most), until the feeler no longer passes; 4. plug the under-carrier cables. Pigtails: dress each one as drawn, with no slack (it rides up with the board when the joint is unplugged): straight up out of the socket, toward the front about 12 mm over the board beside U5A (J9 on the right), out between the P03 and the motor face, and down to the inline joint just ahead of the motor (x 15.2..17.8, |y| 38..60); then trim each wire at its own cavity of the male housing (finished lengths 35.4–60.8 mm for J4 and 31.1–56.5 mm for J5, set by where each wire sits at both ends) and crimp its male pin into the 1×6 housing, red wire = pin 1. Factory cables: measure each one from the encoder cap to the female housing's rear face (the wire entry); readings of 186–200 mm all fit (2–3 turns), and a longer cable up to 220 mm still fits (up to 3.5 turns). Route the fixed path first (about 89 mm outside the coil): a flat row along the motor's inner end face toward the rear, round the motor's rear shoulder and forward over the motor top (never over the pigtail), down the motor's front shoulder under the bumper lead, and from the coil position into the housing; wind the remainder (the measured length less the fixed path: 97–111 mm) into the coil on the base ahead of the motor (2–3.5 turns, about 16 mm across, at x 25, |y| 72) and tie it through its two slots. Then mate each motor's factory female housing onto its pigtail's male housing: the joint is not keyed, so mate the pin-1 stripe to the pin-1 stripe (both halves are marked at the red wire) and check the colours run straight across; stand the joint on the base and tie it down with a cable tie down the motor opening and up through the slot beside it; bumpers J10/J11; front cliffs J8/J9; 5. set and verify the P03 output voltage on the bench, connect it to U5A/U5B (pin 1 is "+" on both terminals, silk "+", the screw nearer the robot centre line: U5A.1 to P03 IN+, U5B.1 to P03 OUT+, red wires on pin 1), then fit it on its foam tape in the front bay with the cable tie through the P_base slots at (28, ±33.3); before the Jetson is connected (W04 unplugged): battery in, F1 fitted, rocker on, and measure against a GND pad: U5A.1 reads positive, about the pack voltage, and U5B.1 positive 5.1 V (0 V or negative: the P03 leads are swapped or loose); then rocker off; 6. stand the two rear 20 mm F-F standoffs on the board and screw each down with an M2.5 × 12 countersunk screw from under P_base through the base, the clamp spacer and the board (they clamp the board); 7. fit the Jetson (four M2.5 top screws), then its six plugs; before the 5 V barrel plug goes in, check the Jetson lead W04 on J3 with its barrel plug free and the rocker on: the plug's centre reads positive 5.1 V against its sleeve (negative: the two Micro-Fit crimps are swapped), then rocker off and plug it in. Service: step 0, every time, before reaching inside: shut the Jetson down, switch the rocker off and unplug the battery (BAT+ is live and unfused at F1's input whenever the battery is plugged in). Everyday rule: the rocker off before plugging or unplugging the battery; shut the Jetson down before switching the rocker off; fit or pull a fuse only with the rocker off (rocker off, fit F2, rocker on). With the lid off, the board's rear band (Pico USB, rear connector row, the Jetson 5 V lead J3, fuses) is reachable; the motor inline joints, the other under-carrier connectors and the P03 (tie, trimpot) need the Jetson off (its six plugs: camera, LiDAR and Pico USB, Wi-Fi dongle, 5 V barrel plug, fan; then its four top screws). To take the board out: Jetson off; the two rear standoffs off (their M2.5 screws from under P_base); the battery out (strap, Tamiya plug); the four tray screws out, the tray slid 2 mm aft and lifted straight out (its springs come off the board edge; its walls are cut clear of the rear cliff sensor boards); the four M3 board screws out; unplug the rear-band plugs, the motor inline joints (loosen each factory-cable coil tie first: the 8 mm each housing slides back comes out of the coil; then cut the joint ties and slide each factory housing off its pigtail; the pigtails stay on J4 / J5 and ride up with the board), the bumper and front cliff leads and the P03 leads; lift the board. Fit new ties when it goes back (retie the coils).

name: Rear shell segment left (az 88–187 incl. flange and lap)
note: Fixed (unsensed) rear fender, R152.5 × 2.8 mm wall with a 10 mm 45 deg inner top rim, z 18–98.5, and 3 × 6 mm inner vertical fins (z 35–84, 45 deg lower ends). Print upright on the lower edge, no supports: foot ribs and gussets are solid to the bed, the Ø6.2 counterbores open on the bed face with a 0.3 mm sacrificial bridge (print z 2.45–2.75, two 0.15 mm or one 0.2 mm layer; the screw pierces it, or drill Ø3.4), dowel holes are teardrops. Two foot ribs bear on the base underside; each takes two M3 × 10 pan-head thread-forming screws from below into Ø8 × 5 bosses on P_base (6.5 mm engagement), and carries a 4 mm gusset up the wall to z 68. The shell starts at az ±92.5 just inside the bumper end, ramped from R151.5 to R152.5 over 3.5 deg, and a backer flange closes the slot behind the bumper end. Slicer: 4 perimeters, PETG at about 245 °C with part cooling ≤ 30 % below print z 57.5 (layer adhesion), then a height-range modifier from print z 57.5: fan 50–60 % and 50 % speed for the 45 deg inner rim; 5 mm brim on the arc ends plus mouse ears, reduced speed above print z 47.5. Release test: push at z 98.5 with 30 N on the rear centre, no whitening. Never lift the robot by the shell. Carries the 7 deg lap tongue (4 mm dowel pads) behind the right segment.
